text:
mara: Quick question — hitting friction in SDK surfaces across Python/TS/Go. Proposal: make async-first surface in languages where idiomatic (Python/TS) and provide a thin sync shim; for Go keep idiomatic blocking APIs but share core transport primitives. How do we keep transport-level retry/pagination semantics consistent?

devin: I like async-first for py/ts. Main worry is retries + paginated iterators: if we retry a page request we need resume semantics that are safe and deterministic.

lia: For paginated endpoints servers should return an explicit resume_token (stable id) or a tuple (cursor_id, offset) so retries can re-request without duplication. Client retry should be allowed only when request is marked idempotent.

mara: Thinking SDK core exposes two primitives: send(req, {retry_safe: bool, resume_token?: str}) and iterator.resume(token). Language shims map these to async generators / sync iterators. Does that cover the ergonomics+safety concerns?

devin: That maps nicely. Edge case: streaming responses that yield partial results before server issues a resume_token. Need a client-side checkpointing hook so apps can commit progress.

lia: Exactly — SDK should offer optional checkpoint callbacks: on_checkpoint(token) that app can use to persist progress. Cancellation must also surface an IncompleteStreamError with resume_token when available.

sachin: From transport POV we need a per-request "retry_safety" flag. HTTP and gRPC adapters should translate that into retry logic. Default backoff = server Retry-After (if present) then exp-backoff with jitter. Also expose max-retry budget per iterator to avoid infinite replay.

mara: For language specifics: Python: async generator + sync wrapper that runs loop in threadpool for sync users. TS: async generator + convenience .next() wrapper for sync-like use in some host envs. Go: keep channel/iterator pattern that uses context for cancellation.

lia: Cancellation semantics must be unified: cancel -> abort transport -> surface CancelledError / IncompleteStreamError with optional resume_token. Document behavior clearly.

devin: Implementation note: transports should attach metadata header like `X-Resume-Token` on responses and accept `X-Resume-Token` on requests. That keeps surface consistent across HTTP/gRPC.

eng-bot: Deploy bot: New spec branch opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2965 — sdk async/sync shim + transport resume tokens.

mara: I'll draft the RFC addendum with short examples for py/ts/go. Example (python):
```py
async for item in client.records.list_iter():
    process(item)
# sync wrapper: for item in client.records.list_iter_sync(): ...
```

mara: I'll also add a section on idempotency rules for paginated endpoints and default retry budgets. Ping me if you want to pair on examples.

devin: :thumbsup:

lia: sgtm
